channel.title: JoharTrip
channel.description: Pilgrimages, journeys & travel guides across India

item.title: Ayodhya travel guide
item.description: Ayodhya, one of the seven holy cities, is home to the grand Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Mandir, Hanuman Garhi and the illuminated Ram ki Paidi ghats.

item.title: Badrinath travel guide
item.description: Badrinath, on the banks of the Alaknanda, is one of the original Char Dham and the Chota Char Dham, with hot springs, colourful temple architecture and Mana, India's 'first village'.

item.title: Darjeeling travel guide
item.description: Darjeeling offers sunrise over Kanchenjunga from Tiger Hill, the UNESCO-listed toy train, world-famous tea gardens and Buddhist monasteries.

item.title: Dooars homestays travel guide
item.description: Homestays across the Dooars, from tea-estate villages to forest-edge hamlets near Jaldapara and Gorumara, offer a lowland, wildlife-oriented alternative to the hills.

item.title: Dwarka travel guide
item.description: Dwarka, the western dham, is home to the Dwarkadhish temple, the Nageshwar Jyotirlinga nearby and Bet Dwarka island, now reached by the Sudarshan Setu bridge.

item.title: Goa travel guide
item.description: Goa is India's favourite beach state, with Portuguese-era churches, spice farms, quiet Hindu temples like Mangueshi and Shantadurga, and a relaxed coastal lifestyle.

item.title: Hanle and Changthang homestays travel guide
item.description: Hanle and the Changthang plateau in eastern Ladakh offer homestays and astro-stays near the Indian Astronomical Observatory, with Tso Moriri, Kiang herds and nomad culture nearby.

item.title: Haridwar travel guide
item.description: Haridwar is one of the seven holy cities and a Kumbh Mela site, famous for the evening Ganga Aarti at Har Ki Pauri and as the starting point of the Char Dham yatra.

item.title: Jaipur travel guide
item.description: Jaipur, a UNESCO World Heritage City, offers Amber Fort, Hawa Mahal, the City Palace, Jantar Mantar and the revered Govind Dev Ji temple.

item.title: Jibhi and Tirthan Valley homestays travel guide
item.description: Jibhi and the Tirthan Valley, near the Great Himalayan National Park, are known for wooden homestays, river walks, waterfalls and quiet village life in the Banjar region of Kullu district.

item.title: Kamakhya (Guwahati) travel guide
item.description: Kamakhya temple on Nilachal hill in Guwahati is one of the most important Shakti Peethas and the centre of Tantric worship, famous for the Ambubachi Mela.

item.title: Kedarnath travel guide
item.description: Kedarnath, highest of the twelve Jyotirlingas, sits beneath snow peaks at the head of the Mandakini valley and is reached by a mountain trek from Gaurikund.

item.title: Kinnaur homestays: Sangla, Chitkul and Kalpa travel guide
item.description: Sangla, Chitkul and Kalpa in Kinnaur offer homestays among apple orchards, wooden temples and views of the Kinner Kailash range.

item.title: Kolkata travel guide
item.description: Kolkata pairs the Kalighat Shakti Peetha, Dakshineswar and Belur Math with colonial heritage, legendary food and UNESCO-listed Durga Puja.

item.title: Lava, Kolakham and Rishyap homestays travel guide
item.description: A cluster of quiet hill villages in the Kalimpong district where homestays run by local families are the main way to stay, with forest walks, sunrise views and home-cooked Himalayan food.

item.title: Markha Valley trek homestays travel guide
item.description: The Markha Valley trek near Leh lets trekkers stay in village homestays along the route, eating with local families and crossing high passes with views of the Stok Kangri range.

item.title: Nubra Valley and Turtuk homestays travel guide
item.description: Nubra Valley villages such as Hunder, Diskit, Sumur and Turtuk offer homestays among apricot orchards, with monasteries, sand dunes and a distinct Balti culture at Turtuk.

item.title: Parvati Valley homestays: Kasol, Tosh and Kalga travel guide
item.description: The Parvati Valley villages of Kasol, Tosh, Kalga and Pulga offer homestays, guesthouses and hostels with river views, forests and treks to places like Kheerganga.

item.title: Puri travel guide
item.description: Puri, one of the Char Dham, is home to the Jagannath temple, the Rath Yatra chariot festival and a long golden beach on the Bay of Bengal.

item.title: Rameswaram travel guide
item.description: Rameswaram, on Pamban island, is both a Char Dham and a Jyotirlinga, famous for its 22 sacred wells, the longest temple corridors in India and the ghost town of Dhanushkodi.

item.title: Rishikesh travel guide
item.description: Rishikesh combines ashrams and Ganga Aarti with river rafting and mountain cafes, and is the gateway to Neelkanth Mahadev and the Himalayan pilgrimages.

item.title: Sham Valley homestays: Alchi, Likir and Ule travel guide
item.description: The Sham Valley west of Leh has low-altitude villages and monasteries such as Alchi and Likir with homestays that suit acclimatisation and short village-to-village treks.

item.title: Sandakphu and Singalila trail stays travel guide
item.description: The Singalila ridge trek to Sandakphu uses village homestays and simple trekkers' lodges at Maneybhanjan, Tumling, Kalipokhri and Sandakphu, with Himalayan views including Kanchenjunga.

item.title: Sittong homestays travel guide
item.description: A low-altitude hill village in the Darjeeling district with family-run homestays, orange orchards and views of the Kanchenjunga range, popular as a quieter alternative to Darjeeling.

item.title: Somnath travel guide
item.description: Somnath, traditionally the first of the twelve Jyotirlingas, stands on the Arabian Sea coast at Prabhas Patan, with an evening light-and-sound show and the Triveni Sangam nearby.

item.title: Spiti Valley homestays travel guide
item.description: Spiti's high-altitude villages such as Kaza, Kibber, Langza, Komic and Dhankar offer homestays where Spitian families host travellers in traditional houses, with monasteries and star-filled skies.

item.title: Tirupati & Tirumala travel guide
item.description: The Sri Venkateswara temple at Tirumala is among the most visited shrines in the world, famous for its darshan system, hair-offering tradition and laddu prasadam.

item.title: Ujjain travel guide
item.description: Ujjain is home to the south-facing Mahakaleshwar Jyotirlinga, its unique dawn Bhasma Aarti and the Mahakal Lok corridor, and hosts the Simhastha Kumbh on the Shipra.

item.title: Vaishno Devi (Katra) travel guide
item.description: The holy cave of Mata Vaishno Devi on the Trikuta mountains is reached by a well-paved trek of about 12-13 km from Katra, with ponies, battery cars and helicopters for help.

item.title: Varanasi (Kashi) travel guide
item.description: One of the oldest living cities on earth, Varanasi is home to the Kashi Vishwanath Jyotirlinga, the evening Ganga Aarti and more than eighty ghats along the holy river.
